 State Police issue nearly 2,000 citations, make 16 OUI arrests during ‘Operation Wicked Safe’
 Troopers inspected nearly 600 trucks and commercial vehicles and found more than 1,300 serious violations, State Police said.
 By Samantha Genzer 
 October 20, 2026 | 5:51 PM

 State Police issued more than 1,900 citations and made 16 OUI arrests in Massachusetts during a multi-state crackdown on dangerous driving last week, the agency said. 
 The initiative, dubbed “ Operation Wicked Safe ,” ran from Oct. 13 to 16 and deployed targeted patrols across major northeastern roadways. Police in Connecticut, New Hampshire, New York, Rhode Island, and Vermont also participated. 
 In Massachusetts, officers stopped 3,714 motor vehicles. Citations were issued for speeding, distracted driving, seat belt violations, and other traffic offenses, State Police said in a news blog . 
 “Operation Wicked Safe sent a clear message that dangerous and distracted driving will not be tolerated on our roadways,” State Police Colonel Geoffrey Noble said. “Our Troopers see firsthand the risks created by excessive speed, distraction, impairment, and reckless behavior.” 
 Advertisement: Troopers also inspected nearly 600 trucks and commercial vehicles, identifying more than 1,300 serious violations, State Police said. 
 Those included suspended operators, false logbooks, drivers driving without a license or without an ignition interlock device, controlled substances in vehicles, and improperly adjusted brakes, the agency said. 
 Troopers additionally made three commercial vehicle arrests and issued more than $72,000 in fines, per State Police. 
 The five other participating states reported approximately 2,000 traffic citations, 78 distracted driving violations, more than 900 speeding tickets, and 20 OUI arrests, State Police said. 
 “By coordinating our efforts with five neighboring agencies, we expanded our enforcement presence across state lines and reinforced our shared commitment to protecting everyone who travels our roads,” Noble said. “While this operation focused on select dates, the State Police will continue to hold dangerous drivers accountable every day of the year.”
